newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm but no reshuffle impact seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm but no reshuffle impact seen.

text.p: MinFin bonds were steady at higher levels on Tuesday compared with Friday and dealers said the government reshuffle announced on Tuesday was already priced in. Monday, March 10, was the Women's Day holiday in Russia.
Dealers said current prices are differing by just up to 0.20 point from Friday's close.
President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday ordered a full reorganisation of the Russian government, leaving only Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and First Deputy Premier Anatoly Chubais in place.

"What is important is that Chernomyrdin and Chubais are staying. The latter is a reputed reformer so the impact on the market was neutral, at most. It (the reshuffle) has been priced in anyway," Aljba Alliance Bank dealer Sergei Seryogin said.
He added MinFin prices are more dependent at the moment on U.S. Treasuries.
Dealers said some feverish selling started right after the news but it was brief and did not affect prices which are sticking to morning levels.
"The day is rather calm. The market is waiting for New York's reaction (to the government reorganisation) and it is expected to be positive," Mosbiznesbank dealer Igor Potapov said.
